subject: SIG: logging evidence & tenant log-access procedure

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acmebank.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: michael.sommers@acmebank.com
Date: 2026-01-18T09:05:00Z
Subject: SIG follow-up - event logging, retention, customer access

Jonas,

Thanks for the quick answers in the SIG spreadsheet. Security team has a couple of follow-ups specific to audit logging so we can close the control narratives for logging and monitoring:

- Can you provide a concise list of event types you log (auth events, model inference, admin changes, billing events, etc.)?
- Confirm the default retention period for tenant-level audit logs and the retention options available to customers. We need explicit retention durations (e.g., 90 days, 13 months, etc.) and whether they are configurable.
- How can a customer access their logs? We need the exact process (API, support request, console export) and any SLAs for providing exports.
- Are exports redacted to remove other tenants' metadata or PII by default? If so, please describe redaction/segmentation approach.
- Please attach one sample log export (sanitized) and the policy document that governs log retention and deletion.

Appreciate a short packaged response we can include in the SIG answer column. If this needs to go to their compliance team directly we can loop them in.

Laura Chen
Senior Information Security Manager
Acme Financial Services
security@acmebank.com

Date: 2026-01-18T12:01:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG follow-up - event logging, retention, customer access

Jonas / Evelyn — draft below with links to the artifacts. I attached sanitized sample export and the retention policy PDF to this thread. Also included a small note on redaction. Feel free to edit before I send to Acme.

--- DRAFT ANSWER (for SIG spreadsheet) ---
Event types captured (representative):
- Authentication and authorization events (login, API key use, OAuth token exchange)
- Administrative/config changes (role changes, config updates, model pin/rollout changes)
- Inference request metadata (request ID, model variant, token count, prompt/response hash, latency metrics)
- Billing and quota events (usage meter ticks, quota-limit hits)
- System/health events (agent restarts, autoscaler actions, node failures)

Retention and options:
- Default tenant audit-log retention: 13 months from event timestamp.
- Shorter retention tiers available by request: 90 days, 180 days.
- Longer retention (up to 36 months) available under contract for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Retention policy and deletion schedule described in attached: audit-log-retention-policy-2025.pdf

Customer access and export process:
- Hosted customers: Console -> Audit Logs -> Export (CSV/JSON) for the selected date range (self-serve).
- Dedicated/private customers: API endpoint (POST /audit-logs/exports) or support request for managed export. API exports are generated on-demand and written to a customer-specific S3 bucket (role-based access).
- For both models, exports are tenant-scoped and delivered within 48 business hours for support requests; console/API exports are asynchronous and typically available within minutes to a few hours depending on range.
- If an on-demand export includes fields that are considered PII or cross-tenant metadata, the export pipeline applies tenant scoping and redaction rules (see redaction notes).

Redaction/segmentation approach: 
- All exports are filtered by tenant_id at query time; cross-tenant metadata is never present in tenant-scoped exports.
- Fields marked sensitive (full prompt text, certain user-supplied PII) are redacted by default in exports unless the customer has contractually accepted retention of unredacted data (rare). Redaction examples attached: log-redaction-example.png

Attached artifacts: sample-log-export-20260104.csv (sanitized), audit-log-retention-policy-2025.pdf, log-redaction-example.png

Operational notes:
- Support ticket for exports: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/ACME-4127 (we create one on behalf of acme if they ask).
- API docs: https://api.redwood.ai/docs#audit-logs-exports (internal link in answer column).

--- end draft ---

Priyom Das
Manager, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SIG follow-up - event logging, retention, customer access

Laura — thanks for the questions. Pulling from our platform docs and the artifacts attached, please find a concise set of answers you can paste into the SIG spreadsheet. Files attached: sample-log-export-20260104.csv (sanitized), audit-log-retention-policy-2025.pdf, log-redaction-example.png.

1) Event types (representative)
- Authentication/authorization: API key use, login events, token issuance/revocation.
- Admin/config changes: role assignments, policy changes, model version pinning/rollouts.
- Inference metadata: request_id, model_id, model_variant, token_count, latency_ms, request/response hashes (not full open-text).
- Billing/quota: usage meter increments, quota-threshold alerts.
- Platform health: node up/down, autoscaler actions, background job failures.

2) Retention
- Default tenant audit-log retention: 13 months.
- Options: 90 days and 180 days (shorter), and up to 36 months under contract for Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Retention behavior and deletion schedules are documented in the attached PDF (audit-log-retention-policy-2025.pdf).

3) Customer access / export process and SLA
- Hosted: self-serve export from Console -> Audit Logs (CSV/JSON) for selected ranges; export job typically completes within minutes for short ranges.
- Dedicated/Private: POST /audit-logs/exports (customer API) to request an export, or raise a support ticket. Exports are generated on-demand and delivered to a customer-owned S3 bucket or via secure transfer.
- SLA for managed support exports: 48 business hours from ticket creation; self-serve/API exports are asynchronous and usually available in minutes–hours depending on size.

4) Redaction / tenant segmentation
- Exports are tenant-scoped at query time; we never include other tenants' metadata in a tenant export.
- Sensitive fields (full prompt/response text where applicable) are redacted by default from exports unless a customer has agreed to retain unredacted content under contract. See attached redaction example (log-redaction-example.png).

If you want, we can provide an additional sample containing a longer date range (up to 90 days) — that would need a managed export ticket. Otherwise the attached sanitized CSV should illustrate format and column names for the SIG response.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Head of Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1-415-555-0123
